Latest primary filings reviewed:
- **8-K / Exhibit 99.1, published 2026-11-09**: Sanmina reported **Q4 FY26 revenue of $3.86B**, **FY26 revenue of $14.53B**, **FY26 operating cash flow of $944M**, **FY26 free cash flow of $541M**, and **Q4 ending cash and cash equivalents of $1.68B**. - **10-Q for quarter ended 2026-06-27, published 2026-07-27**: Sanmina said it had **$1.845B cash and equivalents**, **$2.2B debt outstanding**, **$600M available under Term Loan A**, **$1.5B available under the revolver**, and **$71M of foreign short-term borrowing capacity**; it also said it was **in compliance** with covenants as of quarter-end. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))

Debt / liquidity / covenant takeaways:
- The post-ZT financing schedule is **not** a short-dated balance-sheet crunch: the amended credit agreement extends the revolver and Term Loan A maturity to **2031**, while **Term Loan B matures in 2032**; the term-loan amortization schedule includes a **2030 “balloon-like” step-down**, but the contractual maturity wall is still years away. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanm-20261027.htm))
- Covenant headroom is **not fully quantified** in the filings I reviewed, but the company disclosed a **maximum total net leverage ratio of 4.0x** and **minimum cash interest coverage of 3.0x** covenant, and said it was compliant as of June 27, 2026. I did **not** find a filed post-amendment leverage ratio calculation. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))
- Receivables sales are a real liquidity source, but they are **not cash on hand**; sold receivables are removed from the balance sheet and cash is reported through operating cash flow. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))

Comparable historical price:
- The only comparable historical price I could verify from a primary market source was **$176.48 on 2026-10-19** on Nasdaq Dorsey Wright. I could not verify a full current quote history table from Nasdaq because the page data was unavailable. ([dorseywright.nasdaq.com](https://dorseywright.nasdaq.com/reports/database/menu/stocktype/1/date/2026-10-19/new_all/1/rpt/90/allprice/0/all_scales/1/sourcerpt/))

Unsupported assumptions in a 50% recovery case:
- Assuming the **FY27 outlook midpoint** is achieved without integration slippage from ZT.
- Assuming receivables sales and working-capital conversion remain as strong as recent periods.
- Assuming the amended facility’s covenant headroom remains adequate under stress without a filed calculation.
- Assuming no material dilution, refinancing cost, or customer-demand setback. Those are **not** supported by the filings I reviewed. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanmina_exx991xoctober32026.htm))

Bottom line:
- I see **evidence of operating strength and liquidity**, but I do **not** have enough primary-source support to underwrite a **supported 50% recovery** case from here. The main missing verification is a post-amendment covenant headroom calculation and more detail on ZT integration / cash conversion after the latest quarter. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanmina_exx991xoctober32026.htm))

([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/88205/000008820526000060/q32026pressrelease.htm))
- **Cash generation:** nine-month 2026 operating cash flow from continuing operations was **$180.3 million**, and free cash flow from continuing operations was **$100.7 million** after capex. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/88205/000008820526000060/q32026pressrelease.htm))

The filing also shows **$737.3 million** of available revolver capacity after **$760.0 million** of domestic revolving borrowings and letter-of-credit reserves. - **Debt maturity / refinancing context:** the senior credit facilities have a **final maturity of 2026-09-09-2030**; the 2025 annual report also shows debt maturities concentrated later in the schedule and separately identifies **finance leases** and **operating lease liabilities**. Finance lease obligations are not the same as operating leases. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/88205/000008820526000061/spxc-20260926.htm))
- **Support for resilience:** the business is still growing, cash generation is positive, and near-term contractual liquidity appears ample relative to current debt due within 12 months. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/88205/000008820526000060/q32026pressrelease.htm))

1. **Current valuation math** based on the untrusted snapshot price/market cap is not primary-source verified.  
2. **Any upside forecast** that relies on multiples, terminal margins, or future FCF beyond the filed guidance is an assumption, not a fact.  
3. **Treating adjusted EBITDA as cash flow** would be unsupported; the filings distinguish it from operating cash flow and free cash flow. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/88205/000008820526000060/q32026pressrelease.htm))

- Convertible-note overhang is shrinking: at quarter-end, only **$141M principal** remained outstanding; the company said it expects most holders to convert before redemption, and the redemption notice calls for cash redemption of any notes still outstanding on **2026-11-16**. - I can support the **Nov. 16, 2026** redemption date and the company’s **expectation** that most notes convert, but I cannot verify from the retrieved sources how much will actually convert versus redeem, so dilution remains **partly unresolved**. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/106040/000119312526389859/d23939d8k.htm))
- I can support that the revolver matures in **January 2027**, but not the ultimate refinancing terms, because those are not in the retrieved filings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/106040/000162828026066933/wdc-20261002.htm))

([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/106040/000162828026066882/a4ex991-pressreleaseq127.htm))

**Bottom line**
- There is **good primary-source evidence** that Western Digital’s near-term liquidity is manageable and that the convertible note overhang is being addressed.
